comments.body: Off-by-one. currBlock starts at 0 (bzip2recover.c:398), and the check `currBlock >= BZ_MAX_HANDLED_BLOCKS - 1` (441) runs before `currBlock++`, so the abort happens on the 50000th magic match, not after 49999. Confirmed by building bzip2recover.c: 49999 concatenated 0x314159265359 patterns give "couldn't find any block boundaries"; 50000 give "appears to contain more than 50000 blocks".
Same off-by-one as in the .md: the abort happens on the 50000th match (bzip2recover.c:398, 441-442).

This holds only without -f. With -f, BZ_DATA_ERROR_MAGIC on a later stream jumps to trycat (bzip2.c:465, 506-517), which rewinds the input and appends all of it, as §9 item 18 says. Please qualify the bullet ("without -f") and cross-reference §9.18 so the two sections agree.

last.summary:
Overall this is a careful, well-cited inventory. The diff only touches projects/bzip2/docs/surface-area.{md,json}, and `check_surface.py --only-docs` passes (24 public functions, 35 exported symbols, 23 macros, 2 types, 11 programs).

I checked these claims against the cited source lines, and they are correct:
- BZ2_bzCompress transition table (bzlib.c:407-464): BZ_RUN with no progress gives BZ_PARAM_ERROR (425); an unknown action in RUNNING gives BZ_PARAM_ERROR (439-440); BZ_FINISH with no progress gives BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR (456-457); FLUSH/FINISH fall through via goto preswitch.
- BZ2_bzCompressInit does not range-check verbosity (159-162), and 0 maps to workFactor 30 (164). BZ2_bzDecompressInit checks that small is 0/1 and verbosity is 0..4 (501-503).
- BZ2_bzReadOpen parameter checks, including nUnused 0..BZ_MAX_UNUSED (1103-1108). BZ2_bzReadGetUnused resets lastErr, so a second call gives BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR (1231-1240). BZ2_bzRead returns BZ_UNEXPECTED_EOF on an empty file.
- BZ2_bzWriteClose64 steps 1-7, including the patched `!abandon && ferror` check and the silent BZ_OK when lastErr != BZ_OK.
- BZ2_bzBuffToBuffCompress returns BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR for sourceLen==0 and *destLen==0. I traced it through handle_compress.
- bzopen mode parsing and its 1..9 clamp; bzerror clamps positive codes to 0.
- Decoder validation in decompress.c: origPtr > 10+100000*bs (261-264), nGroups 2..6, nSelectors >= 1, selector >= nGroups (297), excess selectors ignored (299-306), code lengths 1..20 (327), N >= 2M (396), cftab checks (497-522). Assertion codes and their lines in blocksort/huffman/compress/decompress.
- The bit writer drains only before adding bits (compress.c:58-78), so up to 31 bits stay in the buffer after a flush.
- bzip2 option parsing: two passes, long flags override short ones, `-s` caps the block size at 2, `-c` with `-t` exits 1. BZIP2/BZIP token truncation at FILE_NAME_LEN-10 = 1024. Exit-code paths (panic=3, crcError/EOF=2, configError=3, SIGSEGV handler 3/2). trycat rewinds and copies the whole input.
- Makefile install: bunzip2/bzcat are copies; the scripts get symlinks.
- Manual citations behind discrepancies 1, 2, 7 and 15 (manual.xml:1176-1180, 1252-1256, 1574-1576, 2471-2482).

One factual error (an off-by-one), which I confirmed by compiling bzip2recover.c:
- bzip2recover's block limit. The doc says it "aborts with exit 1 once 49999 magic-pattern matches ... have been seen". In the code, currBlock starts at 0 (bzip2recover.c:398), and the check `currBlock >= BZ_MAX_HANDLED_BLOCKS - 1` (441-442) runs *before* currBlock++. So the abort happens on the 50000th match. A file of 49999 back-to-back block magics ends with "couldn't find any block boundaries"; one with 50000 ends with "appears to contain more than 50000 blocks". Please fix the .md (line 1104) and the JSON exit_codes entry (surface-area.json:2076).

Minor (please fix while you are there):
- §7.1, the concatenated-streams bullet (md:1069-1072), says a later stream with bad magic is always reported as trailing garbage and counts as success. That is only true without -f: with -f, bzip2.c:465 jumps to trycat, as your own §9 item 18 says. Qualify the bullet with "without -f" and point to §9.18.
- JSON: BZ2_decompress has a non-empty `returns` but an empty `errors` list. Fill in BZ_DATA_ERROR_MAGIC, BZ_DATA_ERROR and BZ_MEM_ERROR with when they occur, as you did for the public functions. BZ2_bz__AssertH__fail's `source` is bzlib.c:41, but the .md says bzlib.c:40-86. Make them agree.
